meta.title: Interactive Children's Music Book - Repertoire Roadmap
meta.canonicalScope: Repertoire curation, catalogue growth, tune-family deduplication, and production status.
precedence: AUDIO-DIRECTION.md remains canonical for audio policy.
DESIGN-HANDOFF.md remains canonical for implementation architecture.
This roadmap does not authorize samples, recordings, modern arrangements, or unverified scores.

scalePolicy.launchFloorMeaning: Minimum serious catalogue, not a cap and not a declaration that all 120 must ship on the first public day.
scalePolicy.countingRule: Count distinct composition objects or tune-family objects only. Alternate lyrics/titles, instrument renderings, excerpts/full modes, arrangements, and page placements do not create extra catalogue counts.

pianoReductions.note: Right hand is the catalogue melody. Left hand is a root-fifth bass in a declared key, not a concert edition. Identity left-hands (Moonlight, Pachelbel, Joplin) are still generic bass.

statusWorkflow.meaning: Interesting title only; no approval implied.
Fits the project and may enter the catalogue after duplicate checks.
Composition/tune, exact version, source edition and jurisdiction review are recorded.
Authoritative source and representation mode are locked.
Playable data exists but has not been checked musically against the source.
Pitches, rhythm, structure and source relationship have been checked.
Verified data, grouping, art and child-facing copy are shipped.
Potentially useful but blocked by rights, source, cultural, technical or editorial uncertainty.
Do not add unless the owner explicitly reopens the decision.

evaluationCriteria.question: Will a child or parent recognize it, or is the melodic identity unusually strong?
Does it add a composer, form, instrument, rhythm, texture, period, place or cultural tradition not already overrepresented?
Can it generate movement, characters, place, weather, story or a memorable visual concept?
Can the exact composition/tune and an acceptable source be documented conservatively?
Is its educational and experiential value worth the complexity of a correct score representation?
Does it improve the whole library rather than merely adding another similar famous work?

expansionLanes.description: Add secondary but distinctive works to composer rooms that already have a child-facing identity.
Add new rooms or a Discovery Gallery for composers not represented in the 120 floor.
Expand by documented regional modules rather than a random international grab bag. Each module needs exact-variant and cultural review.
Add strong familiar melodies that passed exact-version and rights review but were not necessary for the first 120.
Broaden beyond Christmas into New Year, birthdays, ceremonies and region-specific seasonal music, without duplicating tune families.
Choose pieces because they teach a distinct instrument, form, texture or listening idea, not just because the composer is famous.

agentRules: Treat 120 as the minimum baseline, never as a closed canon or hard cap.
Do not promote a candidate directly to production. Move it through the recorded status workflow.
Do not count alternate titles or lyric traditions as separate songs when they share one tune family.
Do not count Famous Melody and Full Piece as separate catalogue entries.
Do not count the same score rendered through different instruments as separate entries.
Keep stable IDs once an entry is referenced by code, art, notes, tests or documentation.
Never set score verification true merely because playback succeeds.
Lock exact version and source before transcription; lock grouping before page art.
New art follows the final page journey, not the raw catalogue order.
Rights review must distinguish composition, arrangement, recording and edition/transcription.
A candidate with unresolved rights, source, cultural or attribution issues stays on hold rather than being guessed into the catalogue.
Update both the Markdown roadmap and JSON companion from the same data change.
